title: Multiplication by d on an abelian variety is finite locally free of degree d^{2 dim}

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-degree-multiplication-by-d (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 1985-1990

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: choose an ample L symmetric up to [-1], so N = L (x) [-1]^*L is ample and [d]^*N = N^{(x)d^2} by the pullback lemma; a proper curve in a fibre of [d] would carry the ample trivial module N^{(x)d^2}|_C of degree 0, contradicting the curve-degree lemma, so fibres are zero-dimensional and [d] is finite; smoothness of A makes A regular Cohen-Macaulay, whence [d] is flat and thus finite locally free; the degree formula follows from the standard identity deg([d]) deg(N) = deg([d]^*N) read off the Hilbert polynomial coefficient (source lines 1992-2040)

core_obligations: Symmetric ample module (proof lines 1993-2003): A projective (0BFA, 0B45) gives ample L; N = L (x) [-1]^*L is ample (0890) and satisfies [d]^*N = N^{(x)d^2} (0BFF).
Finiteness (proof lines 2005-2014): a proper curve C inside a fibre would make N^{(x)d^2}|_C = O_C ample of degree 0, contradicting 0B5X; fibres are zero-dimensional, so [d] is finite (02OG).

Flatness and degree (proof lines 2015-2040): A smooth (0BFC) hence regular (056S) hence Cohen-Macaulay (00NQ), so [d] is flat (00R4) and finite locally free (02KB); the degree formula follows from 0BEX applied to [d] and the Hilbert-polynomial description of deg(N^{(x)n}) and deg(N).
proof_roadmap: Construct the symmetric ample module N with [d]^*N = N^{(x)d^2} (proof lines 1993-2003).
Rule out positive-dimensional fibres to get finiteness (proof lines 2005-2014).
Deduce flatness from smoothness and read the degree off the polynomial identity (proof lines 2015-2040).
